広いゲイン調整幅内はどのゲイン域も妥協しないサウンドに加え、EQの追加によりサウンドメイクに幅を持たせ、さらにＱの狭いミドルピークの特徴的なブーストスイッチを備え、ミニサイズながら多用途、多目的に使用できる本格ドライブペダルです。 ギタリスト大賀好修氏、伝説的ギターテックhakkai氏との共同開発モデル。 sources.excerpt: Aftermath of 【 Ovaltone / FAT PLEXI 】｜Teddy EG 投稿 ログイン 会員登録 SYSTEM NOTICE Auto translation by AI. Be sure, accuracy, nuances and authorial intent may not be fully reflected. Show original Aftermath of 【 Ovaltone / FAT PLEXI 】 4 Teddy EG 2026年7月28日 09:58 As an Amazon Associate, Teddy EG earns from qualifying purchases. " Trying out Plexi-style pedals #2 【 Ovaltone / FAT PLEXI 】 " In the article, I struggled so much with creating a sound with this distortion pedal. I have finally conquered it. Probably. The environment I tested it in remains the same as this. Gt. (Single-coil P.U.) → 【MXR YJM308】 → 【FAT PLEXI】 → 【AMP】Roland JC-22 What I did was turn on the WH-BOOST. Doing so adds a half-wah sound element, but from there, I dared to use extreme EQ settings. I took the boosted and cut frequencies from turning on the WH-BOOST and, while not fully returning them to their original state, I forced them back with the EQ! This was the key. WH-BOOST on VOLUME 9 o'clock GAIN 1:30 o'clock BASS MAX MID 0 TREBLE 12 o'clock The preceding 'MXR YJM308' is set to LEVEL MAX, GAIN 3 o'clock. It's a huge success!!! It sounds amazing!!! It's a modern Yngwie-esque sound. I adjusted the EQ to try and negate the effect of turning on the WH-BOOST, but the resulting tone, which doesn't quite return to the original, is exquisite. Feeling inspired, I used the rear humbucker and FAT PLEXI as a booster as well. The subsequent stage is the Marshall-style distortion pedal 'Sound Wave Lab / ULTIMATE DRIVE' set to Plexi mode crunch. This pedal is simply the best Marshall-style distortion and allows for switching between 3 modes. The amp is a JC-22. WH-BOOST is on VOLUME MAX GAIN 1-2 o'clock BASS MAX MID 0 TREBLE around 9 o'clock Ovaltone / FAT PLEXI Sound Wave Lab / ULTIMATE DRIVE It's the best!! When I chug on the open 5th and 6th strings, it's crunchy and juicy distortion. It's like Doug Aldrich during his Whitesnake days. I can only play riffs, but I find myself playing "Still of the Night". I almost sold it because I couldn't master it, but I feel like I've managed to conquer it somehow. However, it's a very difficult pedal for me to master, so I would like to continue researching it a bit more. PLAY LOUD!
